summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense/unbound) as the authoritative DNS resolver for node2 and node3, with blocked.example and all its subdomains returning NXDOMAIN via unbound's native DNSBL policy engine, while normal names resolve correctly. Verified persistence and recovery after a one-at-a-time restart of every node.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) and confirmed unbound is the active resolver on port 53; discovered node2/node3 (Ubuntu 24.04) were using the platform gateway (10.100.113.1) for DNS, not node1
Added an unbound DNSBL blocklist policy to node1's /conf/config.xml via a Python XML edit (blocklists=blocked.example, wildcards=blocked.example, nxdomain=1, no source_nets restriction)

Applied the change via configctl unbound dnsbl (regenerated /var/unbound/data/dnsbl.json) and configctl unbound restart; verified via the dnsbl_match.py test tool and live drill queries that blocked.example and arbitrary subdomains return instant local NXDOMAIN while unrelated domains resolve normally
Configured node2 and node3 to use node1 (10.100.113.10) as DNS server via a systemd-networkd drop-in (DHCP UseDNS=no + static DNS=10.100.113.10), applied with networkctl reload
Verified end-to-end resolution from node2 and node3 using resolvectl query: normal names resolve, blocked.example and subdomains do not
Captured pre-restart baseline (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3, plus DNS behavior) for all three nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time using native reboot commands (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled each until exec was available again, and confirmed each node's boot marker changed
Post-restart, re-verified unbound service health and DNS blocking behavior on node1, and DNS resolution behavior on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 provides normal name resolution for node2 and node3
evidence.summary: resolvectl query example.com from node2 and node3 (using node1 as DNS server) returns correct A/AAAA records

evidence.requirement: blocked.example and all subdomains resolve to nothing usable
evidence.summary: dnsbl_match.py confirms the DNSBL policy actively blocks blocked.example and any subdomain; drill and resolvectl queries from node1, node2, node3 return NXDOMAIN / not found for blocked.example and www.blocked.example/foo.blocked.example/sub.blocked.example, while example.com resolves normally

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 actually use node1 as their DNS server (not just reachable)
evidence.summary: resolvectl status on node2 and node3 shows DNS Servers: 10.100.113.10 after installing the systemd-networkd drop-in
kern.boottime, unbound running status, and blocked/normal DNS behavior captured before reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot command acknowledged before disconnect, subsequent exec timed out confirming disruption, kern.boottime changed from 17:49:09 to 17:53:58, and post-restart unbound service plus DNS blocking/resolution verified healthy
boot_id, uptime, and DNS resolution (normal + blocked) captured before reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged, connection reset confirming disruption, boot_id changed from 01c87a03... to b15efec2..., and post-restart DNS resolution (normal resolves, blocked.example NXDOMAIN) verified via resolvectl
boot_id, uptime, and DNS resolution (normal + blocked) captured before reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged, connection reset confirming disruption, boot_id changed from dfeb3b70... to f34262ba..., and post-restart DNS resolution (normal resolves, blocked.example and subdomain NXDOMAIN) verified via resolvectl
